blocks.text:
19 days through Brazil, Argentina, Chile, Bolivia and Peru. Celebrate New Year on Copacabana in Rio de Janeiro, then see Iguazu Falls from both sides, Buenos Aires and Santiago, cross the Atacama Desert and the Bolivian Altiplano in 4x4 jeeps, travel across the Uyuni salt flats, reach Lake Titicaca, Cusco and Machu Picchu, and finish your journey in Lima.

## Prices and accommodation

The tour runs from 30 December 2026 to 17 January 2027: **19 days / 18 nights**. All prices below are **per person for the entire tour**, in US dollars.

| Hotel category | SGL — one person per room | DBL — per person sharing a double room | TPL — per person sharing a triple room |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 4★ | $13,789 | $10,355 | $10,102 |
| 5★ | $16,465 | $11,790 | $11,501 |

**For two people sharing one double room:** $20,710 with 4★ hotels or $23,580 with 5★ hotels. The DBL rate is the price for one participant, rather than the total for two.

Domestic flights listed in the itinerary are included. International flights to and from the tour are paid for separately.

## From Copacabana to Machu Picchu

On your very first evening, Rio will be preparing for the biggest celebration of the year. Stages are set up on Copacabana, white bracelets and flowers appear at the kiosks, and on 31 December thousands of people head to the ocean dressed in white. Fireworks light up the water, music plays on the beach, and flowers and small boats carrying offerings to Iemanja are sent out to sea.

After the celebrations, the route continues across the continent. From Corcovado and Sugarloaf, you will see Rio nestled between granite mountains and the ocean. At Iguazu, you will stand beside an immense line of cascades, with spray hanging in the air and the roar of water drowning out conversation. Buenos Aires brings broad avenues, La Boca, San Telmo, Recoleta and an evening tango show.

Chile begins in Santiago, where the Andes rise behind city blocks and glass towers. Then the city falls behind as the road leads to San Pedro de Atacama, dry air, volcanoes and the desert night sky. This is the start of the high-altitude section: 4x4 jeeps, lagoons with flamingos, geysers, hot springs and the Uyuni salt flats.

Next come La Paz, Tiwanaku, Lake Titicaca and the floating Uros Islands. In Peru, the route takes you through Puno and Cusco to Machu Picchu. The train follows the Urubamba, green slopes draw closer, and the terraces and stone buildings of the Inca city emerge among the mountains. The journey ends in Lima, with its colonial centre, Miraflores and museums.

## Highlights of the route

### New Year on Copacabana

On the night of 31 December, Copacabana's waterfront becomes one enormous celebration. The humid ocean air mingles with music from the stages, people arrive dressed in white, and flowers and small boats with offerings to Iemanja appear at the water's edge. When the fireworks begin, their flashes reflect in the dark water, bathing the whole sweep of the beach in light for a few minutes. This is one of the scenes that gives the New Year departure a real purpose beyond a date on the tour calendar.

### Rio from above

On Corcovado, the entire city opens up before you: granite mountains, the bay, green slopes, beaches and densely packed neighbourhoods. Sugarloaf offers a different, closer panorama. You can make out boats in Guanabara Bay, the Niteroi Bridge, islands and the coastline. These two viewpoints reveal different sides of Rio: first a vast landscape between ocean and mountains, then individual districts and details.

### Iguazu from both sides

From the Brazilian side, the falls form one sweeping panorama. Before you stretch a long line of cascades, humid forest and white spray above the gorge. During the rainy season, the volume of water is particularly high. Paths and clothes quickly become wet even without a downpour, and the roar feels almost physical.

The Argentine side brings you closer to the torrents. Trails run along walkways above the river and beside the ledges, while the ecological train takes you towards the Devil's Throat. At first, the water around you is broad and calm; then an edge appears ahead, beyond which the flow plunges abruptly out of sight. The contrast between the quiet river and the force of the falling water is especially striking here.

### Buenos Aires and an evening of tango

In Buenos Aires, the itinerary brings together several different faces of the city. Plaza de Mayo and Casa Rosada reveal the capital's official history; La Boca and San Telmo add colourful facades, cobblestones, old bars and street life; Recoleta shows a more restrained, elegant side. In Recoleta Cemetery, narrow passages wind between marble family tombs, and the noise of the city almost disappears. In the evening, your introduction continues at a tango show with an orchestra, singers, dinner and Argentine wines.

### Santiago and the Andes

In Santiago, the mountains constantly return to view. On clear days, the Andes stand behind glass towers and residential blocks, appear between streets and open up from viewpoints. The historic centre, with La Moneda and Plaza de Armas, gives way to the modern districts of Vitacura, Las Condes and Providencia. January is hot and dry here, so the change from humid Iguazu and Buenos Aires is immediately noticeable.

### A night in the Atacama

San Pedro de Atacama looks completely different: dusty streets, low houses, dry air and volcanoes on the horizon. After sunset, temperatures fall and the sky becomes the main attraction. On an optional astronomy tour, the group travels beyond the lights of the village. Professional telescopes reveal lunar craters, planets and star clusters. On a moonless night, the Milky Way is particularly clear.

### Highland Bolivia

The road through southern Bolivia crosses the Altiplano, where distances seem immense and familiar landmarks are scarce. At Laguna Verde, the water lies at the foot of Licancabur. Isolated rock formations stand on the empty plain of the Dali Valley. At Sol de Manana, hot steam and sulphurous gases rise from the ground, while several species of flamingo feed in the shallows beside Laguna Colorada.

The next day brings more lagoons, Ollague Volcano, the Chiguana salt flats and the village of Colchani, where salt is collected, dried and prepared for further processing. The road then reaches Salar de Uyuni. In dry weather, white salt patterned with geometric shapes lies beneath the wheels; after rain, a thin layer of water turns the surface into an enormous mirror. The horizon almost disappears, making distances difficult to judge.

### Titicaca and the Uros Islands

Lake Titicaca lies at high altitude, where bright sunshine comes with a cold wind. From Puno, you will travel to the floating Uros Islands. Their foundations and buildings are made from totora reeds. The reeds are laid in layers, the surface gives gently beneath your feet, and the same material is used for boats and roofs. This is a living environment that local families continually renew by adding fresh layers of reeds.

### Cusco and Machu Picchu

In Cusco, Inca masonry remains part of the modern city. Stone walls line narrow streets, with colonial facades above them. During the guided tour, you will see Coricancha, Qenqo, Puca Pucara, Tambomachay and Sacsayhuaman. At the last site, the size of the blocks and the precision of their mortar-free joints are particularly evident.

The journey to Machu Picchu begins by train along the Urubamba. Green slopes gradually draw closer, then the road climbs in hairpin bends. The city itself opens up among humid mountains: terraces descend the slope, steps and squares run between them, and stone walls connect residential and ceremonial areas. Here, you can clearly see how the Incas used the natural shape of the mountain, reinforced its slopes and channelled water.
